Download as PDF Printable version In other projects Wikimedia Commons Wikidata item Appearance move to sidebar hide From Wikipedia, the free encyclopedia American specialty-coffee retailer and consultant George Howell (born 1945) is an American entrepreneur and one of the pioneers of the specialty-coffee movement in the early 1970s. [ 1 ] Early life [ edit ] Born and raised in New Jersey , Howell's family moved to Mexico City when he was 13. He studied art history, French, and Spanish literature at Yale University from 1964 to 1967, when he dropped out. [ 2 ] Career [ edit ] In 1974, Howell and his wife Laurie moved to Boston . After having lived in Berkeley, California , for a time, Howell said, "In 1974 we [decided] to leave the West Coast , I already had two kids with another on the way. We decided to move east to Boston. We drove cross-country. I took with me some whole bean coffee and a grinder. We stopped at the various Howard Johnson’s that were on the interstates on our way

I took with me some whole bean coffee and a grinder. We stopped at the various Howard Johnson’s that were on the interstates on our way and I would go into men’s room, grind the coffee there, leaving it smelling a whole lot better than when I walked in, and then I would take out my French press on the counter, ask for hot water for 35 cents and make my French press at the Howard Johnson’s counter. And within minutes I would always have several people around me wondering what that was, and this is before I even had any clue that I would get into a coffee business." [ 3 ] Coffee Connection [ edit ] In 1975, Howell founded Coffee Connection , [ 4 ] a coffee shop and retailer in Cambridge, Massachusetts which was a pioneer in third wave coffee . It expanded to 23 locations in the Northeast. [ 2 ] It was acquired by Starbucks Corporation for $23 million in 1994 (equivalent to $50 million in 2025), [ 5 ] [ 2 ] and formed the nexus of their expansion into the Boston area. With the

With the acquisition, Starbucks acquired the rights to use the name Frappuccino for a popular blended iced coffee drink, [ 2 ] which Starbucks reformulated. In 2012, Howell founded George Howell Coffee . [ 2 ] [ 6 ] [ 7 ] [ 8 ] Its first location was in Newtonville, Massachusetts , and as of 2026 [update] it is a mini-chain with five locations in the Boston area. [ 1 ] Professional activities [ edit ] In 1997, Howell was invited to become a quality consultant to Brazil as part of the Gourmet Project, a 2-year initiative set up by the United Nations ’ International Trade Council (ITC) and the International Coffee Organization (ICO), which influenced the creation of the Cup of Excellence competition.
